title: Quieter, More Compact Than Cuisinart; But Cuisinart Has More Advantages
text:
Quieter, More Compact Than Cuisinart; But Cuisinart Has More Advantages. I wondered whether this TRIPLE SCOOP 1.5 QUART ICE CREAM MAKER (TS-562-Red; about $59 on Amazon) would be an improvement over my much-used [[ASIN:B003KYSLMW Cuisinart 1.5 Quart Ice Cream Maker]] (about $48 on Amazon). The answer is "Yes and No", but mostly "No".

+++Yes, the Triple Scoop is quieter (a lot quieter); it takes up less storage space (freezer tub and motorized lid only; no separate motor base and big plastic cover); and it freezes the ice cream slightly harder (at least when you use the Triple Scoop ice cream mix (one vanilla, one strawberry, one chocolate packet included).

+++No, the Triple Scoop has a too-small, too-narrow spout for adding ice cream mix (the mix spills unless you're very careful or you use a funnel); the finished ice cream is difficult to remove from the paddle (most of the ice cream comes out with the paddle, too); the Triple Scoop motor element is difficult to remove from the clear plastic lid for cleaning (the motor element plus lid is also hard to grip when you're attaching it to the freezer tub); the Triple Scoop has no recipes for making ice cream from scratch with your own ingredients (the instructions say to buy the Triple Scoop ice cream mix packages).

The two machines make about the same quantity of "soft-serve" ice cream (put it in the freezer if you want more solidly frozen ice cream). Both machines use freezer tubs that must be placed in a freezer for 24 hours for best results. (Note that if your ice cream isn't freezing, you can't just run the machine longer than the recommended 20 minutes or so, because the tubs warm up during use.) The freezer tubs are hand-washable only (because they contain something liquid that freezes hard in the freezer). None of the Triple Scoop parts are dishwasher safe; some of the Cuisinart parts are dishwasher safe.

The notion that you need to purchase Triple Scoop ice cream mix to make homemade ice cream is kind of ridiculous. All you need for ice cream is 2 cups of milk, half-and-half, or heavy cream, plus some sugar and flavorings. You can use recipes from anywhere, as long as you don't overload the motor by adding two many extra ingredients like chopped fruit or nuts. I tried the included Triple Scoop Strawberry ice cream mix, and didn't care for it. It tasted like strawberries, but also faintly like artificial flavoring and preservatives (so it's not for anyone who wants to avoid the chemical additives in commercial ice cream).

Overall, I much prefer my very noisy, storage-space-hogging, Cuisinart ice cream maker (shown with a purple tub from an all-purple model).
